project.title: Standardising Pharmacy Front-of-House Workflow and Stock Layout
project.objective: Design and roll out a standard workflow and shelf layout to improve medication safety, stock accuracy, and customer experience across the pharmacy.
deliverables: Documented standard operating procedures for front-of-house pharmacy tasks
Standardised shelf layout plan for medicines and health products
Medication storage and labelling guideline for prescription and OTC areas
Customer interaction and health education quick-reference guide
Training checklist and completion log for all assistants and shelf fillers
constraints: All procedures must comply with healthcare and pharmacy legislation
Changes must not disrupt opening hours; implementation done in low-traffic periods
Shelf layout must respect storage conditions and safety separation rules
Documentation must be understandable for new staff with minimal supervision
Stock movement must be traceable during relabelling and re-shelving

risks.risk: Misplacement of medicines during re-shelving causes dispensing errors.
risks.mitigation: Use a step-by-step checklist, double-check high-risk medicines, and have a pharmacist validate critical sections.

risks.risk: Staff do not consistently follow new standard operating procedures.
risks.mitigation: Provide short training sessions, visible quick guides, and periodic spot checks with feedback.

risks.risk: Implementation interferes with customer service during peak hours.
risks.mitigation: Schedule layout changes for off-peak times and split work into small, time-boxed tasks.

risks.risk: Non-compliance with storage and labelling regulations.
risks.mitigation: Cross-check guidelines with pharmacist and health and safety officer before rollout and adjust if needed.

themes.why_relevant: All changes must maintain or improve safety and comply with healthcare legislation.
Clear, logical layout reduces picking errors and improves customer experience.
SOPs align how assistants and shelf fillers handle routine tasks.
New processes must be easy to learn and apply consistently by all staff.
Assistants must give clear, compliant information while workflows change.

themes.theme: Coordination between assistants and shelf fillers
themes.why_relevant: Smooth handover between stock handling and dispensing reduces errors.

backlog.task: Map current front-of-house workflow for prescriptions and OTC requests
definition_of_done: Current steps from customer arrival to medication handover documented
Pain points and safety risks listed
Validated by at least two pharmacy assistants

backlog.task: Design standard shelf layout for prescription-only and OTC medicines
definition_of_done: Draft layout map created for all key categories
High-risk medicines clearly separated and highlighted
Layout reviewed with a pharmacy assistant and pharmacist

backlog.task: Create standard operating procedure for receiving and storing new stock
definition_of_done: SOP covers checking deliveries, storage conditions, and expiry dates
Includes steps for documenting discrepancies
Reviewed for compliance with organisational guidelines

backlog.task: Develop medication labelling and shelf labelling guideline
definition_of_done: Guideline defines label content, font size, and placement
Rules for changing shelf labels documented
Approved by pharmacist or health and safety officer

backlog.task: Prepare training checklist for new workflow and layout
definition_of_done: Checklist covers all new SOPs and layout rules
Includes sign-off fields for each staff member
Reviewed with store manager for practicality

backlog.task: Pilot new shelf layout in one section of the pharmacy
definition_of_done: Selected section re-shelved according to layout plan
Before/after photos captured
Issues and adjustments logged after one week of use

backlog.task: Draft quick-reference guide for customer communication at the counter
definition_of_done: Key phrases for common health queries documented
Guidance on informed consent and privacy included
Guide fits on one page for easy use at the counter

backlog.task: Define process for handling and documenting near-miss incidents
definition_of_done: Near-miss definition and examples documented
Simple reporting steps created
Aligned with existing incident reporting requirements

backlog.task: Create daily checklist for shelf fillers to verify stock and labels
definition_of_done: Checklist includes stock levels, expiry checks, and label accuracy
Time estimate per aisle documented
Tested for one week and refined based on feedback

backlog.task: Coordinate implementation schedule to avoid peak hours
definition_of_done: Peak and off-peak hours identified for each day
Implementation slots agreed with store manager
Schedule shared with all assistants and shelf fillers

backlog.task: Update storage practices for temperature-sensitive medicines
definition_of_done: List of temperature-sensitive items confirmed
Storage locations and monitoring steps documented
Checked against healthcare legislation and guidelines

backlog.task: Summarise project outcomes and remaining follow-up actions
definition_of_done: Short summary of changes and benefits written
Open issues and next steps listed
Shared with pharmacist and store manager

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on current issues and approve target workflow scope
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message asking for main pain points and confirming what the new workflow must cover

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on the list of front-of-house processes to be standardised in this project.
Prioritise top three pain points to address first in the new workflow.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Define and approve the standard shelf layout and labelling rules
threads_plan.trigger: Shelf filler shares draft layout map and asks for feedback from assistants

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the initial standard shelf layout for pilot section.
Confirm labelling rules for high-risk and temperature-sensitive medicines.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Lock in SOPs for stock reception and daily checks
threads_plan.trigger: Pharmacy assistant posts draft SOP steps and daily checklist for review

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the SOP for receiving and storing new stock.
Approve the daily shelf and stock verification checklist format.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Agree on training approach and rollout schedule
threads_plan.trigger: Message proposing training checklist and suggested implementation times

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm training format and who must complete the checklist.
Approve the implementation schedule to avoid peak hours.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Review pilot results, near-miss logs, and finalise follow-ups
threads_plan.trigger: Post summarising pilot feedback and any incidents or near-misses observed

channel_rituals: Daily short async check-in on which section or SOP each person is working on
Twice-weekly update thread on layout and labelling issues found during shifts
Weekly review of near-miss log and quick adjustments to checklists or SOPs
Pre-close-of-day note when any shelf or workflow change might affect next shift
End-of-project summary thread capturing lessons learned and remaining actions
